sentences.text:
Sudati Surender Rao , Sudhakar Rao, ... vs Chinthala Narahari,
Warangal City And ... on 21 July, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Namavarapu Rajeshwar Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1153 Of 2015
Judgment:

This M.A.C.M.A is filed by the appellant/petitioner under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
aggrieved by the order and decree dated 04.03.2014 passed in M.V.O.P.No.1091 of 2009 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District Judge, Warangal (for short "the Tribunal").
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties will be hereinafter referred to as they are arrayed before the Tribunal.
3.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District Judge, Warangal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that the petitioner filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 15.10.2007.

3.1. On 15.10.2007, the petitioner during the evening was proceeding from Shyam Nagar along with a 2 RRN,J pillion rider by his motorcycle bearing No.AP-36R-3077, when they crossed the Rupireddypally bus stage at about 4.15 p.m., the driver of the Jeep bearing No.AP-15K-5060 (for brevity, crime vehicle) drove it at high speed in a rash and negligent manner proceeding from Bhupalpally to Parkal side and dashed against their motorcycle, due to which, he and the pillion rider fell down on the road.
The petitioner sustained a closed head injury, injury on the right forearm, fracture of the right femur, and fracture of both bones of the right leg.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Parkal, and from there he was shifted to Jaya Hospital, Hanamkonda.
As he was immediately admitted to the Hospital for the treatment, and as his family members were attending him, they could not lodge a complaint immediately.
But, his father lodged a complaint on 30.10.2007 with the SHO, P.S. Regonda.

The SHO, Regonda after a thorough investigation filed a chargesheet against the driver of the crime vehicle holding that he was 3 RRN,J rash and negligent while driving the jeep and was responsible for the accident.

3.2 The petitioner was admitted as an inpatient on 16.10.2007 in Jaya Hospital, Hanamkonda and later, he was shifted to Osmania General Hospital, Hyderabad, on 17.10.2007 and admitted in the Hospital till 10.11.2007.
Thereafter, he was shifted to Aditya Hospital, Hanamkonda on 10.11.2007 and he continued his treatment as an inpatient up to 15.12.2007.
Again, he was admitted as an inpatient on 19.09.2008 in City Orthopedic Hospital, where he underwent an operation and got removed implants on 20.09.2008 and he was admitted till 01.10.2008.
Even after the said discharge, the petitioner is still unable to attend to his normal duties and he is constantly taking treatment.
Due to fractures sustained by him, he became permanently disabled to the extent of 40%.

1 his income to the tune of Rs.4,37,500/-
4 RRN,J during the period of his treatment.
Hence, the claim petition.
4. Respondent No.1 remained ex parte before the Tribunal.

Respondent No.2/Insurance Companies filed counter by denying all the material averments and contended that the driver of the crime vehicle did not possess a valid and effective driving licence, and that the vehicle was not road worthy to ply, and that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent and immature driving on the part of the petitioner without following road rules.

They further contended that there is an inordinate delay in lodging the complaint and it clearly shows that the petitioner in collusion with the owner of the jeep, falsely implicated the jeep to claim compensation.
Hence, prayed for the dismissal of the petition.

5. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
i) Whether the accident was due to rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Jeep bearing No.AP-15K-5060?
5 RRN,J ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, at what amount and from whom?
iii) To what relief?
6.
The petitioner to prove his case, examined PWs.1 to 5 and got marked Exs.A1 to A16 and Ex.X1 to X7.
On behalf of respondent No.2, neither oral nor documentary evidence was adduced.
7. After considering the evidence available on record, the Tribunal allowed the claim petition in part by granting Rs.4,53,600/- to the petitioner towards compensation.
Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, the present appeal.

8. Heard both sides and perused the record.
9.

Learned Counsel for the petitioner contended that the Tribunal erred in deducting 1/3rd of the income of the petitioner towards his living expenses and as the case on hand is one that of an injury,
there is no question of deducting any portion of income towards personal expenses.
It has also been contended that the monthly income of the petitioner was taken at Rs.3,000/-, which is very meagre.

He further contended that the compensation awarded under other heads is very 6 RRN,J meagre and prayed to enhance the same by allowing the appeal.
10.
Per contra, learned Counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent would contend that the Tribunal was justified in fixing the compensation and no interference is required by this Court.

Accordingly,
prayed to dismiss the appeal.

2 11.

It has been rightly argued by the learned Counsel for the petitioner that the Tribunal erred in deducting 1/3rd of the income of the petitioner towards his personal/living expenses as the present case is not one that of a death but that of an injury.

Hence, the deduction made by the Tribunal is not sustainable and the total income of the petitioner without any deduction is to be taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of future loss of income on the account of disability.

12. Coming to the earnings of the petitioner, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the petitioner at Rs.3,000/- per month considering the age of the petitioner as 31 years, and the petitioner failed to prove that he sustained loss in agriculture.
However, the petitioner contends that he 7 RRN,J being an agriculturist was earning Rs.2,00,000/- per annum.
The petitioner also filed some receipts of Tak Patties issued by the Market Yard committee, which show that the petitioner received a sum of Rs.5,235/- on 16.4.2007.

In the absence of any concrete proof, this Court is inclined to fix the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.4,500/- p.m. in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramchandrappa vs Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.1.

entities.text: Ramchandrappa vs Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The annual income of the petitioner would come to Rs.54,000/-.

The petitioner was aged 31 years at the time of the accident, thus, the appropriate multiplier for the purpose of calculation of loss of earnings due to disability is '16' as per Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Road Transport Corporation2.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Road Transport Corporation2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the loss of future earnings due to disability at 40% comes to Rs.3,45,600/- (Rs.54,000 x 16 x 40%).
13.
The Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner under the head 'pain and suffering'.
Keeping in view the gravity of the injuries and the prolonged suffering even after a year of the accident, this Court is inclined to award Rs.75,000/- towards the said head.

It is 1( 2011 ) 13 SCC 236 2 (2009) 6 SCC 121.
8 RRN,J observed from the impugned order that the Tribunal awarded Rs.1,80,000/- to the petitioner towards medical bills, by rounding off the same from Rs.1,83,126/-.
This Court is of the opinion that such rounding off and granting compensation on the lower side despite there being cogent evidence is unjust.
Hence, the petitioner is awarded Rs.1,83,126/- towards medical bills.
The petitioner was awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/- and Rs.10,000/- towards injuries and transportation charges etc.
The same is reasonable and thus calls for no interference.

14. In all, the petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.6,73,126/- (Rs.3,45,600 + Rs.75,000 +
Rs.60,000 + Rs.10,000 + Rs.1,83,126).
15.
It is further noticed from the impugned order that the petitioner was awarded interest on the compensation @ 6% p.a.
The same is hereby increased to 7.5% p.a as the Hon'ble Courts are time and again granting interest on the compensation amount at 7.5%.

16. Accordingly, the M.A.C.M.A. is allowed by enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal 9 RRN,J from Rs.4,53,600/- to Rs.6,73,126/- (Rupees Six Lakh, Seventy Three thousand,
One hundred and twenty six only) with interest @ 7.5% from the date of petition till the date of realization.

The respondents shall deposit the said compensation amount together with interest and costs after giving due credit to the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

Upon such deposit, the petitioner is permitted to Sudati Surender Rao , Sudhakar Rao, ... vs Chinthala Narahari, Warangal City And ... on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5973446/
3 withdraw the entire amount.
